summary: The idea is sound and safe because the per-(tclass, window) graph-timed prepare gate falls back to master. The realistic gain is about 0-60 us at first_turn and about 0 at turn_1, which is inside the +-1.5% CI, so read the result from the [qkv-split] GATE lines and the per-shape rows, not the headline. Two build fixes are needed or the gate will very likely turn every key OFF, or measure a serialised schedule: relax the byte-identical KV parity check, and address block-scheduler starvation of FA3 by the gate GEMM.
justification: The mechanism is plausible but oversold. The FLOP numbers check out. qkv at T=16384 is 618 GFLOP; the 192x192 nvjet trio of 2530 us (qkv + o + one of pooler/unpooler, 1993 GFLOP) gives 788 TFLOP/s, so qkv is about 785 us. At T=753, qkv is one of the three 128x192 calls, not the 112x128 kernel: the 112x128 kernel is the o projection (dense-gemm-cublaslt-algo-pick-prefill-t attributes it the same way). It is 72 CTAs on 132 SMs, about 34-39 us. (1) GEMM efficiency. At T=753 the unsplit GEMM already runs as one partial wave with full K=8192 per CTA. Split, the main N=1280 GEMM (6x7=42 CTAs at 128x192) runs one CTA's full-K time, about the same wall time as the whole qkv today, unless cuBLAS switches to split-K or stream-K. So turn_1 has ~0 critical-path gain and the gate should turn it OFF. At T=3012, N=1280 with the 192x144 tile is 16x9=144 CTAs, 1.09 waves (bad quantisation), against 256 CTAs (1.94 waves) unsplit; main drops from ~150 us to maybe 90-100 us, not 85. At T=16384 with 192x192, N=1280 pads to 1344 (5% waste) and N=1024 pads to 1152 (12.5% waste). cuBLAS may pick better-fitting 128-wide N tiles, but expect the two GEMMs together to cost 2-5% more GEMM-seconds than 785 us (~15-40 us). (2) What the overlap can reclaim. Total tensor work is conserved. Under FA3 (hdim 64, ~2048 CTAs at ft sliding, large smem) a 192x192 4-stage GEMM CTA (~196 KB smem) cannot share an SM, so concurrency here partitions SMs; it does not overlap within an SM. The ceiling is the low-occupancy window: qk_norm 31-43 us, the FP8 casts and store_cache, plus wave tails, about 50-80 us at ft. That is far from the claimed -100 to -200 us. The router-under-pooler precedent is a tiny N=512 GEMM and does not transfer. Net at ft sliding (weight 138) is roughly -60 to +20 us of 11120, so under 0.5%. (3) WEAKEST LINK: block-scheduler ordering. The gate GEMM becomes ready at the same time as qk_norm, and at T=16384 it has ~516 long CTAs (~100 us each). By the time FA3 is ready, the hardware dispatcher still holds a deep queue of pending gate-GEMM CTAs on an equal-priority stream (master's side_stream is a default-priority torch.cuda.Stream). FA3, which is on the critical path, then waits for most of the gate GEMM's waves to drain. The schedule degenerates to serial, with qk_norm squeezed, and the split losses come on top. The prepare gate will catch this (the result goes flat, not a loss), but then the scored submit buys nothing. Fix in the build: give the attention chain the higher priority. Run qk_norm..FA3 on a new high-priority stream (torch.cuda.Stream(priority=-1 or the device's greatest priority), forked from and joined back to main) with the gate GEMM on the default-priority side_stream. Verify in prepare that the captured graph keeps the priority (CUDA 12 records stream priority as a kernel-node priority attribute during capture). If it does not, log it; the gate still decides. (4) The expected directions are consistent with the shape weights: ft sliding dominates the first_turn load, and the turn rows are rightly marked small or flat.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity: it introduced state['side_stream'] for the router under the pooler. This change reuses it earlier in the graph. That is correct (the router's side_stream.wait_stream(main) comes after this change's join), but the two now share one stream, so any later change that moves router work earlier would serialise behind the gate GEMM. No measurement confound today.

align-two-phase-all-t-rega / experts-turn-rega-s4-port-t4096 / experts-turn-rega-s4-first-turn-n128: these touch only the expert path, after the attention front. They shrink the denominator (making a fixed-us gain slightly larger in relative terms) but do not interact with the qkv/FA3 window. Not a confounder.
No landed hypothesis touches the qkv GEMM, FusedQKNorm, store_cache, FA3 or o_norm_gate. The attention front is master's parity code, so a moved attention-front row is attributable to this change.
interference: No companion. The hypothesis carries its own in-process A/B: the prepare gate times master's attention front against the split front as captured graphs, with cold L2, interleaved, per (tclass, window), and prints both us and the ratio. Those GATE lines say what this run would add, and the PATH CHOSEN line says which shapes actually ran split. With those lines and the per-shape rows the result is interpretable whatever its sign. A flat headline with GATE ON at ft sliding showing ~3-5% front savings means it worked but is below headline resolution. GATE OFF everywhere means the overlap does not pay (or the parity check tripped). A scored companion (e.g. control with the gate forced ON) would not resolve anything the GATE lines do not, and costs a scored run. COLLISIONS with in-flight work: (a) fa3-full-contiguous-kv-triton-gather-gated (running) edits the same kernel_fn span: it adds torch.empty k_buf/v_buf, the _kv_gather_contig launch after store_cache, and a different FA3 call on full layers, between this change's fork and join. Expect a textual merge conflict. Semantically, the full-layer GATE decisions here are measured on master's paged FA3. If fa3-contig lands first, rebuild on it and re-gate the full keys; if this lands first, fa3-contig's gate must time its candidates with the gate GEMM running on the side stream. Its own follow-up idea (a prefix KV gather on a side stream under the qkv GEMM) contends for the same idle window and the same side stream. Do not stack the two without re-gating. (b) pre-expert-norm-fused-rega-gather, experts-rega-pingpong-consumers-all-t and experts-rega-producer-scale-expand-all-t are disjoint (expert path) and stack cleanly. (c) dense-gemm-cublaslt-algo-pick-prefill-t (queued, hold) picks a cuBLASLt algo for qkv_gate at N=2304. That is mutually exclusive with this split on the qkv keys, so whichever lands second must re-pick or re-gate. (d) boundary-overlap-s1-slice-kernel-ffn-tail (queued) uses its own bnd_stream on the FFN tail at T>4096 and is disjoint in time. Both raise prepare time (~15 s here, plus the fa3-contig gate, plus bnd's ~40 s), so keep the total under the 300 s prepare limit.
rules_flags: No rule problem found. A row slice of the BF16 qkv_gate weight is a lossless repack that stays BF16; activations stay BF16; the KV cache and q FP8 are unchanged; every key is still attended; branching is on tokens/config only; nothing derived from data is cached; is_current_stream_capturing() is a host-side check and does not sync.

Fork/join under capture: side.wait_stream(main) and main.wait_stream(side) are torch's event record/wait. That is the correct capture fork/join, and the side stream joins main before o_norm_gate, well before capture ends. The side stream must fork from the capturing stream before its first launch, as specified; otherwise capture raises. The prepare-gate graphs must use the same fork pattern on the capture stream. If a high-priority attention stream is added (see justification), it needs the same wait-in / wait-out pair.

record_stream: qkv.record_stream(side) outside capture is correct. attn_input.record_stream(side) is harmless but unnecessary because the join precedes any free; it does touch a harness-owned tensor's allocator bookkeeping, so prefer dropping it to avoid an 'touches harness' reading.

The out= column slices (stride (2304, 1)) are accepted by ATen's addmm as ldc=2304 without a copy, and the main and gate tiles write disjoint columns (the epilogue/TMA store is bounded by N), so there is no write race. The profiler proof in prepare is a good guard.
open_questions: PARITY CHECK WILL MISFIRE: 'k/v cache rows byte-identical, OFF beyond 0.1% of rows' is too strict. If cuBLAS picks split-K or stream-K for N=1280 (likely at T=753, and possible at 3012), bf16 outputs differ by 1 ulp in a fraction of elements. With 128 FP8 values per row, nearly every row then flips at least one FP8 byte, and every key goes OFF for a numerically irrelevant reason. Replace it with a tolerance check: dequantised K/V cache rows rel L2 <= 1e-2 vs master and worst row <= 5e-2 (the judge allows 8%), plus the existing o_norm_gate <= 2e-3. Print the fraction of differing rows for information only.

Does the captured graph keep stream priority (kernel-node priority attribute) on this driver/CUDA? If not, is there another way to stop the gate GEMM's pending CTAs from delaying FA3? One option is to make the gate GEMM depend on store_cache rather than qkv_main, so FA3 and gate become ready together. The gate should time both fork points (after qkv_main and after store_cache) and keep the faster one.

One full-layer gate key covers ft ctx 0, 32768 and 65536 (measured at 32768). FA3 is 0.9 ms at ctx 0 and 8 ms at ctx 65536, so the ratio may differ across them. Consider keying full ft by round(ctx/16384) as fa3-contig does.

The mechanism text attributes the T=753 qkv to nvjet 112x128 at 39 us, but that row is the o projection; qkv is one of the three 128x192 calls (~34 us). This does not change the conclusion that turn_1 will gate OFF.
With fa3-full-contiguous-kv-triton-gather-gated running now, decide the landing order before building, so this build is not rebased onto a changed FA3 call site mid-run.
